newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - Oct 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - Oct 24.

text.p: NOTE: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted, and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

- With 250 days to go before the British colony reverts to China, editorials in the Hong Kong media concentrated on the draft laws governing the People's Liberation Army garrison, which gives Hong Kong courts limited jurisdiction over PLA troops, and the selection manifesto of Tung Chee-hwa, a contender for the post of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region chief executive.
The Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO said the PLA Garrison Law draft embodied the "one-country, two-systems" principle.
It said it reflected China's sovereignty over Hong Kong and and the judicial autonomy to be enjoyed by the future Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

The English-language HONGKONG STANDARD said the draft provided an assurance to Hong Kong people that PLA troops were not monsters. It said, on balance, the promises China had made about the stationing of PLA troops in Hong Kong had been consistent, unequivocal and conciliatory.

The middle of the road HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL said the issue of freedom was not included in chief executive hopeful Tung Chee-hwa's plan for Hong Kong's future, and his attitude towards democracy was conservative, leaning toward gradual democratic development.
It said the only creative element in the manifesto was to the section urging Hong Kong people to get to know more about China, Chinese culture and history.

But it said many elements of Chinese traditional values should be criticised. China was weak for centuries, just because the Chinese clung to a lot of outdated traditional values. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843-6441
